master.title: Turkey issues travel warning for eastern Ukraine amid rising tensions
master.content:
The Turkish Foreign Ministry on Saturday advised citizens to avoid traveling to eastern Ukraine amid escalating tensions between Russia and Ukraine.

“It is recommended that our citizens refrain from traveling to the eastern border regions of Ukraine unless necessary,” the ministry said in a statement.

The ministry also asked people to take all possible precautions for their safety and to contact the Turkish Embassy in Kyiv before essential travel.

On Friday US President Joe Biden reiterated his call for US citizens in Ukraine to leave the country immediately, citing increased threats of military action.

Turkey has recently offered to act as a mediator between Ukraine and Russia to maintain peace in the region.

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan travelled to Kyiv on Feb. 3 in an effort to mediate the crisis with Russia.

After meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, Erdoğan reaffirmed his offer to host a Ukraine-Russia crisis summit in Turkey.

candidate.title: Ukrainian President Zelensky invites US President Biden to visit Ukraine in the coming days
candidate.content:
During a recent telephone conversation, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky invited U.S. President Joe Biden to visit Ukraine in the coming days, the press service of the Ukrainian President reports.

Volodymyr Zelensky, President of Ukraine. Photo: president.gov.ua

Volodymyr Zelensky stressed that the Ukrainian side understands all the risks and is ready for any development of the situation:

“I am convinced that your arrival in Kyiv in the coming days, crucial for the stabilization of the situation, will be a powerful signal and will contribute to de-escalation.”

Zelensky also said that Ukraine is not yet a NATO member, so “only a strong Ukrainian army is a guarantee of state security”.

The phone conversation between Biden and Zelensky took place on Sunday night and lasted about an hour. The leaders reportedly discussed the situation around Ukraine. They exchanged available information and discussed ways of de-escalation and sanctions in case of Russian aggression.
